Inglewood, California
  February 12, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  February 12, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority, and
  Finance Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
  Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a
  quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/Finance
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Joint Powers Authority
  officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
  and Joint Powers Authority

  CONFIRMATION OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS OF THE
  INGLEWOOD POWERS AUTHORITY. The City Council, City Clerk, City
  Treasurer, City Attorney, City Manager, and Assistant City Manager were sworn in as the
  Official Board and Officers of the Inglewood Joint Powers Authority by Aisha
  Thompson, Deputy City Clerk.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority/Finance Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority
  Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the
  City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Joint Powers on
  any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Dotson that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  February 7, 2019, in the amount of $1,518.146.27, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  1
 February 12, 2019

142  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ISSUANCE OF LEASE REVENUE BONDS BY THE
  INGLEWOOD JOINT POWERS AUTHORITY; RESOLUTION NO. 19-31
  ADOPTED. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing
  to receive input on the issuance of lease revenue bonds by the Inglewood Joint Powers
  Authority to refund the outstanding Inglewood Public Financing Authority Lease
  Revenue Bonds, Series 2012, and that notice had been given in the time, form and
  manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file and no communication were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the staff report dated February 12, 2019.

  Sharon Koike, Assistant Finance Director gave a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council.

  There was no response.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Franklin and seconded by
  Council Member Morales that the City Council does hereby Adopt Resolution No. 19-31
  entitled:

  RESOLUTION APPROVING PROCEEDINGS BY THE INGLEWOOD
  JOINT POWERS AUTHORITY FOR THE ISSUANCE AND SALE OF
  LEASE REVENUEBONDS TO REFUND THE OUTSTANDING
  INGLEWOOD PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY LEASE
  REVENUE BONDS, SERIES 2012, APPROVING THE FORM AND
  AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF RELATED DOCUMENTS AND
  APPROVING RELATED OFFICIAL ACTIONS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED.  Letter from the Office of the City Attorney were presented
  recommending denial of the following claims filed by:
  a) Jose Almeida for alleged personal injury/wrongful death on May 10, 2018.
  b) Susana Galarza for alleged personal injury/wrongful death on May 10, 2018.
  c) Elmer Shade for alleged property damage on January 10, 2018 through September 26,
  2018.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  and carried that the above listed claim be denied.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on January 29, 2019,
  be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 142  ONE YEAR BLANKET PURHASE ORDER EXTENSION APPROVED –
  OFFICE DEPOT. Staff report dated February 12, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval of a one-year blanket purchase order extension, for the annual purchase of office
  supplies from Office Depot.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve purchase order extension in the amount of
  $250,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
 February 12, 2019

 178  RESOLUTION NO. 19-32 ADOPTED – REWARD TO ANY INDIVIDUAL(S)
  THAT PROVIDES INFORMATION LEADING TO THE IDENTIFICATION,
  APPREHENSION, AND CONVICTION OF THE PERSON(S) RESPONSIBLE
  FOR THE DEATH OF CRYSTAL CRAWFORD. Staff report dated February 12,
  2019, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution offering a reward to any
  individual(s) that provides information leading to the identification, apprehension, and
  conviction of the person(s) responsible for the death of Crystal Crawford.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla,
  that Resolution No. 19-32 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING A REWARD UP TO $25,000 FOR
  INFORMATION LEADING TO THE IDENTIFICATION, APPREHENSION
  AND CONVICTION OF THE PERSON (S) RESPONSIBLE FOR THE
  HOMICIDE OF CRYSTAL CRAWFORD

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 178  AGREEMENT  NO.  19-108  APPROVED  –  ENTERPRISE  FLEET
  MANAGEMENT. Staff report dated February 12, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval of an agreement with Enterprise Fleet Management to lease/purchase a total of
  fifteen (15) vehicles.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-108 in an amount not to
  exceed $983,454.60. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 178  AGREEMENT NO. 19-109 APPROVED – VirTra, INC. Staff report dated February
  12, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with VirTra, Inc., to
  install and provide support services for one (1) VirTra 300 firearms simulator.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-109 in an amount not to
  exceed 357,422. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  AGREEMENT NO. 19-110 APPROVED – KIMLEY-HORN AND ASSOCIATES,
  INC. Staff report dated February 12, 2019, was presented recommending approval of a
  one-year professional services agreement (with an option to extend one additional year)
  with Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc., to provide design and engineering services for
  the Stadium Alternative Mitigation Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-110 in the amount of
  $1,357,989 (includes a fifteen percent (15%) contingency in the amount of $177,129).
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 142  FISCAL YEAR 2018-2019 FIRST QUARTER BUDGET REVIEW REPORT. Staff
  report dated February 12, 2019, was presenting the Fiscal Year 2018-2019 First Quarter
  Budget Review Report.

  Keauonna Buckhanon, Acting Budget Manager, presented the First Quarter Budget
  Review Report.

  3
 February 12, 2019

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that Resolution No. 19-33 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2018-19 ANNUAL BUDGET

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 219  ORAL REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. City Treasurer, Wanda Brown, thanked
  Keauonna Buckhanon, Acting Budget Manager, for her outstanding Budget Report. She
  stated that she is looking forward to the stadium coming because the City will get 100%
  revenue for property. She thanked Council Dotson for holding his shredding event, and
  stated that the Emergency Preparedness is a great program.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Odest Riley stated that mental health is a serious matter and encouraged everyone to
  check on our boys. He asked the Mayor if he would close the meeting in honor of Xavier
  Patterson, a young man who recently took his own life.

  Stuart Bailey thanked Council Member Dotson, and Council Member Padilla for their
  recent community events. He stated they were both helpful and successful.

  Eric Holey, President of the Inglewood South Bay Chambers, commented that his
  organization will begin to reach out to our youth and get more insight as to what they
  face on a daily basis.

  Ray Davis, 2nd District, extended his condolences to the family of Xavier Patterson, and
  commented that the City of Inglewood is making history every day.

  Willie Agee extended his condolences to the family of Xavier Patterson, and stated he
  would love to see the youth participate more in city activities. He also stated that he is
  proud of what is taking place here in the City of Inglewood.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Xavier Patterson at the hour of 3:00 p.m.

  Approved this 5th day of March, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
